newsitem.title: UK: JFM eyes parallel bond issue ahead of EMU - bankers.
newsitem.headline: JFM eyes parallel bond issue ahead of EMU - bankers.

text.p: Japan-guaranteed JFM is considering launching a parallel Eurobond after its successful debut in French francs, bankers said on Wednesday.
"JFM is thinking about its funding stategy ahead of EMU," Rudolf Lorfing, director at IBJ France told Reuters.
"Today's French franc bond has introduced them to French life insurance companies, and they are now thinking about a parallel bond."
Japan Finance Corp for Municipal Enterprises (JFM) launched a 1.0 billion French franc 10-year bond on Wednesday via joint lead managers Banque Paribas and IBJ France.
The deal had been fully placed with French life insurance companies, Lorfing said. Demand from these institutions was strong, reflecting their desire to diversify their portfolios.
"French life insurance companies are amongst the biggest investors in Europe, and ahead of EMU it is important to be known by them," a Paris-based syndicate manager said.
Since the start of this year, borrowers have been positioning themselves ahead of the introduction of the single currency through launching parallel bonds.
As national currencies are eliminated, investors will increasingly focus on a borrower's credit in deciding what bonds to buy or sell.

Parallel bonds are so-called because they consist of several Eurobonds issued in different European currencies, which, on the introduction of the euro, will redenominate into the single currency and become fungible.
The third stage of European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) is due to start on January 1, 1999 at the latest.
The first parallel bond was launched by Austria in January, and since then a slew of European borrowers have followed.

But to date only European sovereigns and companies like Siemens have tapped the market. JFM is the first non-European entity to eye the market. On the emerging markets side, Brazil has taken bids for a similar transaction.
Lorfing at IBJ said JFM had not taken a decision yet on whether or not to go ahead a parallel bond, "but they like the idea".
